methods.label: Split along the y-axis
methods.explanation:
The shared intercepts make the \(y\)-axis a useful diagonal. First consider the four lines with slopes \(a,b\) and intercepts \(p,q\), where \(a\ne b\) and \(p\ne q\). Set
\[
k=|a-b|>0,\qquad L=|p-q|.
\]
Two opposite vertices are \((0,p)\) and \((0,q)\). Solving for the other two intersections gives their horizontal coordinates as
\[
\frac{q-p}{a-b}\quad\text{and}\quad\frac{p-q}{a-b}.
\]
They lie on opposite sides of the \(y\)-axis, each at distance \(L/k\) from it. The diagonal therefore divides the parallelogram into two triangles, each with base \(L\) and height \(L/k\). Its area is
\[
2\left(\frac12 L\cdot\frac{L}{k}\right)=\frac{L^2}{k}.
\]
The given positive areas ensure that \(a\ne b\) and \(c\ne d\), so this formula applies. For the two parallelograms it gives
\[
(c-d)^2=18k,\qquad (c+d)^2=72k.
\]
Dividing these equations and taking positive square roots yields
\[
c+d=2|c-d|.
\]
Let \(t=\min(c,d)\). Solving this relation shows that the larger of \(c,d\) is \(3t\). Hence
\[
c+d=4t,\qquad k=\frac{(2t)^2}{18}=\frac{2t^2}{9}.
\]
Because \(k\) is an integer, \(9\mid2t^2\). The prime \(3\) must therefore divide \(t\), since its exponent in a square is even. Thus \(t\geq3\), giving \(c+d\geq12\) and \(k\geq2\).

The positive integers \(a,b\) satisfy
\[
a+b=|a-b|+2\min(a,b)\geq k+2\geq4.
\]
Consequently \(a+b+c+d\geq16\). This bound is attained by
\[
(a,b,c,d)=(1,3,3,9),
\]
whose areas are \(36/2=18\) and \(144/2=72\). The smallest sum is therefore \(16\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
